Classic Jewish Bagels

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Makes 12 bagelsPrep 2 hours 30 min (including rising time)Cook 20 min

Bagels are a beloved traditional bread enjoyed in Jewish cuisine, especially during the break-fast meal after Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement. After a day of fasting, bagels provide a comforting and satisfying way to replenish energy, often paired with cream cheese, smoked fish, or other toppings.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) bread flour
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • 2 teaspoons active dry yeast
  • 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) warm water (about 110°F/43°C)
  • 2 tablespoons barley malt syrup or honey (for boiling water)
  • Optional toppings: sesame seeds, poppy seeds, coarse salt

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water. Let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the bread flour and salt. Make a well in the center and add the yeast mixture and vegetable oil.
  3. Mix until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  4. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  5. Punch down the dough and divide it into 12 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a ball.
  6. Poke a hole through the center of each ball with your finger and gently stretch to form a ring about 2 inches (5 cm) in diameter.
  7. Place the shaped bagels on a parchment-lined baking sheet and cover with a towel. Let rest for 20 minutes.
  8. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the barley malt syrup or honey.
  9. Boil the bagels in batches, about 1-2 minutes per side. Remove with a slotted spoon and place back on the baking sheet.
  10. If desired, sprinkle toppings on the wet bagels immediately after boiling.
  11. Bake the bagels for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
  12. Cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a chewier texture, use bread flour rather than all-purpose flour.
  • Adding barley malt syrup to the boiling water gives bagels their characteristic shiny crust and slight sweetness.
  • Serve fresh bagels with traditional toppings like cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, and red onion for a classic Yom Kippur break-fast.
